records.name: The Arts League
records.summary: A contemporary art center in West Philadelphia, also listed as the University City Arts League. Artists teach adult classes and workshops, members can use open studio time, and kids can join an after school art program.
records.what_you_do: Take an artist led class or workshop, join as a member for open studio time, or sign a child up for after school art.

schedule.text: Most adult classes run in six-week sessions, mostly on weeknight evenings, with some weekend daytime options. After school art for grades K to 5 runs on weekdays during the school year: pickup from Penn Alexander or Henry C. Lea Elementary is from 3 to 4 pm, and snack and workshops run from 4 to 6 pm.

cost.text: Six-week adult classes cost $250 to $300, with a $25 materials fee in some. Workshops cost $40 to $205. After school is billed monthly by days per week, and holiday day camps are $125 per day.

first_step.how: Choose a class on the Fall 2026 page that still has open spots and register for it, or use the Register link to enroll a child in after school art.
first_step.basis: Several adult classes are listed for all levels or as beginner friendly, and registration is required for each listed class, so the class pages show exactly how to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adult classes are artist led and meet once a week for six weeks, usually for two hours (pottery sessions run three). Six-week classes cost $250 to $300, and first-time students at some classes pay a $25 materials fee. Pottery students can buy clay and tools ahead of time or in the studio, but outside clay is not allowed. Six-week classes include a free open studio week at the end of the term.
first_visit_tips: Several fall classes showed as sold out when checked, so look for one with open spots on its class page.
Fall class sign up closes October 9 at 5 pm, and workshops close 48 hours before the first lesson, so check each page's cut off.
For weaving and woodcarving, buy the first-time materials fee at least 7 days before the first lesson.

records.notes: Email changed from coordinator@ to director@. The site labels coordinator@ for room rentals and youthprograms@ for after school questions. The membership page gave no prices or steps when checked, so the open studio wording is carried from tier 1 and not re-confirmed. Accessibility, parking and transit are not stated on any page read. Class details come from the fall 2026 page only.

records.name: University Lutheran Church of the Incarnation
records.summary: A Lutheran congregation on Chestnut Street with Sunday worship at 10:30 am and a shorter Tuesday service. Its named programs, such as Feast Incarnate and Music and Arts, are listed without days or times.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday or Tuesday worship, read the first-time visitor page, or ask the office about the named programs.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am. Tuesday worship is listed at 4 pm on the home page and at about 6:15 pm on the visitor page, so call to confirm the time. The named programs are listed on the home page without days or times.

cost.text: Visitors do not need to give when the offering plate comes around.

access.notes: Gluten free wafers for communion are available on request from the pastor.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am, and fill in a welcome card from the pew rack if you want the church to know you are new.
first_step.basis: The church has a first-time visitor page, lets visitors say hello to members after the service, and offers a pew card and an online connection card to say you are new.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10:30 am with Holy Communion and lasts a bit over an hour. The music is hymn based, with organ, strings and winds, and dress is casual. Visitors can say hello to a member over coffee after the service. Visitors do not need to give when the offering plate comes around.
first_visit_tips: The main entrance is on 37th Street Walk, a few minutes from 30th Street Station. The contact page also lists trolley routes 10, 11, 13, 34 and 36 to 36th Street Station, and bus 21 to 37th Street.
On Sundays and evenings, park in the lot behind the church, entered from Ludlow Street. On other days, street parking needs a paid kiosk receipt on your dash.
Children are welcome in worship, but there is no nursery during services. Ushers can give you an activity kit.
Communion is offered at both services. You can stand or kneel at the rail, or come forward and receive a blessing if you prefer not to take communion.

records.notes: Tuesday time conflicts: the home page says 4 pm, the visitor page says about 6:15 pm, and the contact page gives no time. Office hours conflict: the contact page says 9:30 am to 4 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays, while the home page and footer say 11:30 am to 4 pm. The record uses 11:30 am. The contact page gives unilu@uniluphila.org, so the email changed from the tier 1 coordinator@ address, which no page read this pass shows. The site has no dated news, and the anniversary banner shows two different years, so it is not used. Wheelchair access, elevator, hearing loop, ASL and quiet room are not stated on any page read.

records.name: Uptown String Band
records.summary: A Mummers string band that practices in Langhorne, Bucks County, and marches in Philadelphia's New Year's Day parade. Its Tuesday rehearsals are at Uptown Hall, which it also manages as a rental venue, and it hosts public community events there.
records.what_you_do: Join as a dancer, musician, marshal or aide, or walk in on a Tuesday night to watch rehearsal. Members also march in the New Year's Day parade.

schedule.text: Music rehearsals at Uptown Hall on Tuesdays, 8 to 10 pm. Prop and scenery sessions on Sundays, 11 am to 2 pm, at an annex in Fairless Hill, Pennsylvania, starting in October. The band marches in Philadelphia's New Year's Day parade each January 1.

locations.label: Annex in Fairless Hill (props and scenery, Sundays)

cost.text: Dues and fees are not published on the site.

first_step.how: Walk in on a Tuesday between 8 and 10 pm at Uptown Hall to watch rehearsal, or fill out the Join Us form on the band's website with your name, email and membership type.
first_step.basis: Visitors can walk in on Tuesday nights to watch, and the Join Us form is a clear way to start. Musicians take a music test and dancers are placed by the drill director, so the first role depends on skill.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tuesday rehearsal runs from 8 to 10 pm at Uptown Hall in Langhorne, and visitors can walk in to watch. Musicians take a short music test with the music director once they feel ready, and dancers' level is set by working with the drill director. Marshals and aides go over their requirements with the chief marshal, and current members range from about 12 to 75. The page gives no dues.
first_visit_tips: Uptown Hall is in Langhorne, Bucks County, and has two full size parking lots, so plan the drive.
Come between 8 and 10 pm on a Tuesday to see the music rehearsal.
If you play, bring your instrument for the music test. The band lists saxophone, banjo, accordion, upright bass and percussion.
If you do not play, ask about dancer, marshal or aide roles. The Join Us form also offers a social member option.

records.notes: Location: Uptown Hall and the annex are both in Bucks County, and the home page describes the band as based in Parkland, PA. The band marches in the Philadelphia parade, so this stays publish as tier 1 decided, but the owner may want to rule on whether a Bucks County Mummers unit counts as serving Philadelphia. last_sign_of_life 2026-10 is carried from tier 1: today's read of the home page shows an October 3 event and a ParklandFest notice with no year printed, so the year could not be confirmed here. The 2026 parade lineup page prints the year 2026 and lists the band, but no calendar day. No minimum age is stated, so none is recorded.

records.name: Urban Creators
records.summary: A North Philadelphia nonprofit working on food, art and learning. It runs Life Do Grow, an urban farm with a public park, an outdoor classroom and an arts space, and it has hosted programs there since 2011.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on the farm or at a service day, schedule a group service project, or join the email list. Past community workshops covered medicinal herbs.

schedule.text: No volunteer days or events are posted right now, and the events calendar shows none. Volunteer days and group service projects are arranged through the volunteer page and by email.

locations.label: Life Do Grow farm and creative space

cost.text: Volunteering costs nothing. Donations are optional and tax deductible.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer intake form linked from the volunteer page, which asks about your experience, interests and availability, then wait for the team's reply.
first_step.basis: Volunteering starts with an intake form and a reply from the team, and no volunteer days are posted, so the first shift depends on the group's answer.
first_step.what_to_expect: No volunteer days are posted right now, so the first step is the intake form and a reply. Past volunteer days were held on Thursdays and Saturdays at the farm on North 11th Street. The site does not say how long a shift lasts or what the work will be.
first_visit_tips: Dress for outdoor work, since the farm is outdoors.
Ask the group which volunteer day is next, since none is posted.
Group service projects are booked by email, so write to the group before you plan a visit.
Public visiting hours are not stated, so ask before you go to the farm.

records.notes: No events are listed on the upcoming events page or the calendar. Past volunteer days were Thursdays and Saturdays. Past October volunteer days and a radish giveaway at Historic Fairhill's fall festival are listed without a year, so they are not dated here. last_sign_of_life 2024-10 is carried from tier 1; no page read this pass prints that year, so status sits at the edge of probably_active. Email: the footer lists operations@, while the volunteer page lists admin@ and a named staff address on a different domain (phillyurbancreators.org) for group service bookings. Only operations@ is recorded.

records.name: Urban Youth Kings and Queens
records.summary: A Germantown youth sports and enrichment group. It runs baseball, softball, Quickball and basketball, plus after-school programs at partner schools and a summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Families register children for the program they want on the group's site. Adults can coach or mentor through the Get Involved page.

schedule.text: Baseball (ages 7 to 14) and softball (girls 7 to 12) run in spring and fall. Quickball (ages 4 to 6) meets on Saturday mornings from 9:45 to 10:45 am in spring. Basketball (ages 4 to 16) has a winter and a summer season, with weeknight practices and games on Wednesdays and Saturdays. After-school programs run during the school year, and a six-week summer enrichment camp is held each summer.

locations.label: SCH Vare Fieldhouse (basketball practices and games)

cost.text: Winter basketball is $110 for ages 4 to 6 and $185 for ages 7 to 16, uniform included. Summer basketball is $165. Quickball is $85 per spring season. The John B. Kelly after-school program is free with limited spots, and the group says it does not turn a child away for inability to pay.

first_step.how: Open the program page you want, such as basketball for ages 4 to 16, and use its Register button. Winter spots are limited, so register early, or email info@uykq.org to ask first.
first_step.basis: Basketball is open to all skill levels and the group says every child gets a chance to play. Quickball is an intro for ages 4 to 6, and each program page explains how to register.
first_step.what_to_expect: Winter basketball practices run on weeknight evenings starting at 6 pm, with one guaranteed practice a week, and games are on Wednesday evenings and Saturday mornings. Coaches are volunteers, and the winter fee includes the uniform. Quickball teaches hitting, fielding, catching and baserunning, and parents help coaches carry out the lessons.
first_visit_tips: Winter basketball divisions are ages 4 to 6, 7 to 9, 10 to 12 and 13 to 16, so check your child's age group before you sign up.
The winter fee includes the uniform. The site does not list shoes or other gear, so ask.
Basketball games and practices are at SCH Vare Fieldhouse, 8000 East Cherokee Street.
Winter registration is online through the team sign up system, and spots are limited and may close early.

records.notes: The Quickball page shows both a closed registration link and an open register button for spring 2026, so the register step is written generally. The Saturday Quickball time comes from the home page; the Quickball page does not give one. A summer registration closure dated May 31, 2024 on the basketball page is probably outdated and was not used. last_sign_of_life 2026-08 is the summer camp that ran June 29 to August 7, 2026, as shown on the home page; the schedule text does not carry that date. Germantown Warriors and Germantown Lady Warriors appear to be the group's own league names, so they are not listed as leads. Spring 2026 skills clinics are closed and not recorded. Winter 2027 registration is open with a December 13, 2026 deadline, which is a one time date and is not recorded. Mentoring: there is no separate program; adults volunteer as coaches or mentors.

records.name: UrbEd Advocates
records.summary: A youth led Philadelphia group that does organizing and policy work to win more money and better conditions for public schools.
records.what_you_do: Students and young adults can apply for internships, a paid year long fellowship, or organizing roles, testify at school board meetings, sign petitions, or use the Youth Space in Center City.

schedule.text: The careers page lists open internships, a fellowship and staff roles, all marked as hybrid, and roles change over time. Testimony at school board meetings needs a sign up with the school district for the meeting you pick. The Youth Space can be reserved or visited, and its hours are not listed.

cost.text: Joining, testifying and signing petitions are free. The year long fellowship is paid, though the pay amount is not stated.

first_step.how: Use the Meet with us button on urbedadvocates.org to ask how to get involved, or apply to one of the open internship or fellowship roles on the Careers page.
first_step.basis: The site has a contact button, open roles with apply links, and a testimony sign up. Eligibility, hours and pay are not stated, so a first timer needs to ask.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first meeting or how long it takes. Joining, testifying and signing petitions are free, and the fellowship is paid. Roles are listed as hybrid, so some work may happen in person at the Philadelphia office on Locust Street.
first_visit_tips: Read each role's own vacancy page, since the careers page gives only titles and tags.
Ask about Youth Space hours before you visit, since the site does not list them.
If you want to testify, sign up with the school district for the board meeting you plan to attend.
Ask whether a role needs in person days, since the roles are marked hybrid.

records.notes: The careers page lists six hybrid roles with apply links, but gives no pay, deadlines, eligibility or application steps. The tier 1 sentence saying most open roles are for Philadelphia high school and college students is not supported by either page read this pass, so it was removed. The careers page names a Philadelphia office at Locust Street, Suite 1001; it is not confirmed as the Youth Space, so no street address is recorded for the Youth Space. The only printed year on the pages read is 2023 in the copyright line, so no last_sign_of_life month is recorded and status rests on the group still listing open roles.

records.name: US-Ghana Chamber of Commerce
records.summary: A membership trade group that links businesses in the United States and Ghana. It runs trade missions, business summits and open community gatherings, and a youth volunteer program for high school students.
records.what_you_do: Members get trade, investment and networking help and can join trade missions. Public gatherings are open with registration when one is listed, and tri-state high school students can volunteer at large Philadelphia area events through the Youth Diplomats program.

schedule.text: Trade missions, summits and public gatherings are posted on the events page when they are planned, so there is no regular weekly or monthly schedule. Youth Diplomats volunteers work at large Philadelphia area events.

cost.text: Membership dues as listed: $50 for students, $250 for individuals or professionals, $1,500 for club or corporate, and $5,000 for council. The page does not say how often dues are charged. Public gathering prices were not shown on the pages read.

first_step.how: Register for a public gathering through the registration link on the chamber's events page when one is listed, or compare the membership levels on the membership page before you join.
first_step.basis: Membership is aimed at businesses and professionals and costs $50 or more, and the events calendar showed no listed events when checked. Public gatherings open with registration, so the way in depends on the next event.
first_step.what_to_expect: Some public gatherings have included live music, food, networking and a raffle. Membership payments go through an outside payment page, so check the level and price first. Event registration runs through a separate ticket link.
first_visit_tips: Public gatherings use a separate registration link on the events page, not the membership payment page.
The Youth Diplomats program takes applications through a Learn More link, and the page does not list ages or steps.
The chamber lists an office in Philadelphia, but no street address is printed on the pages read, so ask before you visit.

records.notes: last_sign_of_life 2026-05 is the trade mission to Ghana, May 30 to June 5, 2026, as posted by a regional trade center. Its cost and registration status are not stated. The events page showed no listed events for October 2026 and links to a second events page, which was not read. A public gathering on the home page (June 27, Philadelphia) prints no year, so it is not used. The membership page lists office space in Philadelphia and Accra, but no street address is printed. Youth Diplomats 2026 is described as volunteering at large Philadelphia area events; ages and steps are not stated. The World Trade Center Central PA page is a regional trade listing rather than a community group, so it is not added to leads_only.

leads_only.name: Historic Fairhill
leads_only.note: Named by Urban Creators as the partner hosting a fall festival where it gave out radishes. The url is the page that names it; the group's own site was not captured, so it was not checked.

notes: All 7 batch groups checked with 26 WebFetch calls and 0 of 1 WebSearch. No rate limiting, bot checks or blocked pages. Verdicts: publish 7. Open items for the owner: (1) Uptown String Band rehearses and keeps its hall in Bucks County but marches in the Philadelphia parade, so the out_of_area question is open; (2) University Lutheran lists two different Tuesday times and two office hours, and the record flags both; (3) Urban Creators has no dated evidence on the pages read this pass, so its 2024-10 date from tier 1 and low confidence should be re-checked. Largest corrections: Arts League email now director@ (coordinator@ is labelled for rentals); University Lutheran email now unilu@; Urban Youth Kings and Queens now active (summer camp 2026); US-Ghana membership dues are now listed; UrbEd's unsupported eligibility sentence was removed. Leads: only Historic Fairhill was added; LuMin Network (named on the Lutheran home page as an external link, no url captured) was not added.
